abertura: People ask questions in meetings for many reasons.
Three of these sentences are true. Mark the three.

itens.t: People often check dates and numbers in meetings.
itens.porque: Dates and numbers are easy to hear wrong, and a wrong date can cause problems later.

itens.t: A question in a meeting means you were not listening.
itens.porque: People who listen carefully often ask the most questions, because they notice what is not clear.

itens.t: A short question can save time later.
itens.porque: Checking a detail now takes a few seconds. Fixing a mistake next week takes much longer.

itens.t: Only the manager can ask questions.
itens.porque: Anyone in the meeting can ask. The meeting works better when people do.

itens.t: It is normal to ask someone to say something again.
itens.porque: People speak fast in meetings, in any language. Asking again is part of the conversation.

itens.t: You should wait until the end to ask anything.
itens.porque: Some questions are better right away, especially about a date or a number.

sec2.pt: Escolha o sentido que cada expressão tem numa reunião de trabalho. As seis aparecem na reunião que você ouve na aula.

abertura: Listen to the voice message once. Two of these sentences are true. Mark the two.

audio.texto: Hi, this is Sam from Office Plus. I am calling about your order of chairs for the meeting room. The chairs are not coming on Monday. They are coming on Tuesday morning, before ten. If that is a problem, please call me back today. My number is five five five, zero one four two. Thanks.

itens.t: The message is about a change to a delivery.
itens.porque: The chairs are not coming on the day in the order. They are coming one day later.

itens.t: The message is about a problem with a price.
itens.porque: Sam talks about a day and a time. He does not talk about money.

itens.t: Sam wants to hear from you today if there is a problem.
itens.porque: He asks you to call him back today if the new day is a problem.

itens.t: Sam is calling to sell new furniture.
itens.porque: The chairs are already ordered. He is calling about when they arrive.

sec3.pt: Ouça a mensagem de voz uma vez e marque as duas frases verdadeiras sobre o assunto dela.

sec4.titulo: The same message, for the details
abertura: Listen to the voice message again. This time, listen for the details and choose the right ending.

audio.texto: Hi, this is Sam from Office Plus. I am calling about your order of chairs for the meeting room. The chairs are not coming on Monday. They are coming on Tuesday morning, before ten. If that is a problem, please call me back today. My number is five five five, zero one four two. Thanks.

itens.t: The chairs are now coming on
They arrive
If there is a problem, call Sam

sec4.pt: Ouça de novo a mensagem da atividade 3. Agora preste atenção nos detalhes e escolha o final certo de cada frase.

abertura: You call Sam back, but you are not sure about the day. Which answers help you check?

itens.t: Sorry, did you say Tuesday?
itens.porque: It repeats the day you are not sure about, so Sam can answer yes or no.

itens.t: OK.
itens.porque: Sam thinks you understood, and you still do not know the day.

itens.t: Could you say the number again?
itens.porque: It asks for one piece of information again.

itens.t: Yes, yes, thank you.
itens.porque: It ends the call before you check anything.

itens.t: So the chairs come on Tuesday morning, right?
itens.porque: It says what you understood, and asks Sam to confirm it.

itens.t: I don't know.
itens.porque: Sam does not know what you did not understand, so he cannot help.

sec5.pt: Você liga de volta para o Sam, mas não tem certeza do dia. Diga se cada resposta ajuda você a conferir a informação ou não ajuda.

abertura: Write what you would say when you call Sam back.

callout.texto:
Say who you are. Check the day and the time of the delivery. Say if the new day is OK for you.

You can use what you write in your lesson.

sec6.pt:
Escreva o que você diria ao ligar de volta para o Sam.

Diga quem você é, confira o dia e o horário da entrega, e diga se o novo dia está bom para você. Você pode usar o que escrever na aula.

itens.t: The delivery is now one day earlier.
itens.porque: Ryan: “The delivery is now on Wednesday, not Thursday. One day earlier.”

itens.t: The laptops arrive on Wednesday morning.
itens.porque: They arrive on Wednesday, but “in the afternoon, after four.”

itens.t: Someone needs to install the new system.
itens.porque: Ryan: “We need to install it.” Nora starts on Wednesday evening.

itens.t: The training moves to the following week.
itens.porque: Paula keeps the training on Tuesday, with the old laptops.

itens.t: Installing the system takes all day.
itens.porque: It takes “about two hours for all twenty laptops.”

itens.t: Ryan is going to write to the trainer.
itens.porque: Paula asks him to tell the trainer, and he says: “I'll email her today.”

tf2.rationale: The day is right in two of the false sentences, and the detail is wrong: Wednesday afternoon, not morning; two hours, not all day.

itens.t: Sorry, did you say Wednesday?
itens.porque: Paula heard a day, and she is not sure it was Wednesday.

itens.t: Sorry, could you say that again?
itens.porque: The person did not hear the information, so they ask for all of it again.

itens.t: So the laptops can be ready on Thursday morning, right?
itens.porque: Paula puts the information together and asks if her idea is right.

itens.t: Just to check, do the laptops come with the new system?
itens.porque: Nora asks about one thing she needs to know before she can plan.

itens.t: Sorry, I didn't catch that.
itens.porque: Catch here means hear and understand. The person needs to hear it again.

itens.t: So we keep the training on Tuesday, right?
itens.porque: It says the decision in a few words and waits for a yes.

mv2.rationale: Three lines are from the meeting and three are new. Two of each kind: hearing it again, checking one detail, and confirming the whole idea.
